title: TerminologyAnalysis
description: Academic terminology refinement performed before bulk discovery: each seed keyword is audited, the product problem is translated into academic task families, and query families are built with an explicit DIRECT or TRANSFER role.
topic: Integrated evaluation of evidence completeness and omission for temporally evolving multi-source free-form generation, with calibrated selective prediction under non-stationary distribution shift
gap_targets: gap-1: integrated decomposed evaluation of correctness, attribution, evidence completeness, temporal correctness, omission, calibration and abstention
gap-4: evidence completeness for compound claims, partial support, complementary sources and temporally versioned evidence
gap-5: omission evaluation for evolving work items, due information, superseded facts and decision-relevant state
gap-8: calibrated selective prediction for non-stationary free-form communication streams
gap-2: bounded check for any directly relevant workplace benchmark, while retaining its ENGINEERING classification
gap-6: human-review methodology terminology, while retaining target-domain protocol design as ENGINEERING
gap-7: evaluator meta-evaluation and bias terminology, while retaining project-specific evaluator separation as ENGINEERING

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Evaluation of whether generated statements are semantically entailed by, or otherwise consistent with, an input source. It is especially established in abstractive summarization and grounded generation.
seed_audit.main_risk: Many methods test only source consistency and do not test evidence completeness, temporal validity, omissions, calibration or abstention.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Static single-document summarization metrics; NLI-only metrics with no source localization; factual consistency studies reporting one aggregate score.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Evaluation of factual correctness of generated content, either against supplied evidence or external knowledge. Modern work often decomposes long-form output into facts or claims.
seed_audit.main_risk: Factuality against world knowledge can be conflated with faithfulness to the supplied evidence and says nothing by itself about citation completeness or current-state correctness.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Closed-book fact checking; biography factuality with no source attribution; factual QA accuracy; knowledge-base verification unrelated to generated evidence chains.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Whether a generated summary preserves factual meaning and does not introduce unsupported information relative to the source.
seed_audit.main_risk: Faithfulness normally measures unsupported additions, not whether important source information was omitted or whether a fact is stale after later revisions.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Readability, coherence or semantic-similarity evaluation described as summary quality; reference overlap metrics without source-grounded factual assessment.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Evaluation of generated information that is unsupported, inconsistent with the conditioning evidence, or factually false, with definitions varying substantially across subfields.
seed_audit.main_risk: The term is underspecified and often collapses attribution errors, factual errors and unsupported content into one label.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Generic LLM hallucination surveys; hallucination detection without evidence localization; image hallucination; medical hallucination benchmarks with no transferable evaluation structure.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Splitting generated text into independently assessable factual propositions or claims before verification.
seed_audit.main_risk: Decomposition quality can itself introduce errors, and different definitions of atomicity produce different denominators.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Argument mining claim segmentation; legal claim extraction; patent claims; discourse decomposition without factual verification.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Extraction or generation of minimal factual statements intended to be independently verifiable against evidence.
seed_audit.main_risk: Atomicity may destroy dependencies, qualifiers, temporal scope or conjunction semantics needed for compound workplace claims.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Argumentative claim extraction; social-media claim detection for misinformation; subject-predicate extraction with no generation evaluation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Determining whether a claim is supported, refuted, insufficiently supported or otherwise verifiable using supplied or retrieved evidence.
seed_audit.main_risk: Classical verification usually treats a fixed claim and static evidence, rather than evaluating whether a generated report cited all necessary evidence.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Misinformation classification with no evidence; stance detection; static FEVER-style verification used without any connection to generation or evidence completeness.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Evidence-based verification of factual statements, often framed as support/refute/not-enough-information classification.
seed_audit.main_risk: The literature is dominated by external-world fact checking rather than source-bounded generation evaluation.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Fake-news classification; social-media misinformation detection; knowledge-base completion; claim credibility scoring without traceable evidence.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Evaluation of whether generated statements are correctly attributable to identified supporting sources.
seed_audit.main_risk: Attribution correctness can be measured without determining whether every citation-worthy statement has evidence or whether the evidence is the current version.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Authorship attribution; quote attribution; speaker attribution; source credibility classification.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: In grounded generation, identification of which source supports a generated statement; outside that context the term commonly means authorship or media-source identification.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase has several large unrelated literatures and therefore needs generation, evidence or citation qualifiers.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Authorship attribution, plagiarism detection, news-source identification, quotation-speaker attribution, forensic source attribution.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Whether an attached citation actually supports the claim or statement to which it is attached.
seed_audit.main_risk: Correctness of existing citations does not test whether uncited claims should have been cited.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Citation formatting; bibliographic metadata correction; citation intent classification; citation recommendation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A measure of whether provided citations are relevant, necessary or genuinely supportive rather than extraneous or incorrect.
seed_audit.main_risk: Definitions differ across benchmarks, and high citation precision can coexist with severe missing-evidence errors.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Information-retrieval precision over scholarly citation recommendation; bibliometric precision measures unrelated to generated claims.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Whether generated statements that require evidence are accompanied by sufficient supporting citations.
seed_audit.main_risk: Some work treats any single supporting citation as complete even when a compound claim needs multiple complementary pieces of evidence.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Bibliography completeness; citation-network coverage; citation presence metrics that do not inspect claim support.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Usually the fraction of citation-worthy generated statements or claims for which appropriate supporting citations are supplied.
seed_audit.main_risk: The denominator depends on identifying citation-worthy propositions and may ignore partial support or multiple-source requirements.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Scholarly recommendation recall; retrieval recall of papers; citation-link prediction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Assessment of whether generated content is supported by provided context or external evidence.
seed_audit.main_risk: Groundedness is not standardized and is frequently used as an umbrella metric that collapses support, attribution and factuality.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Vendor-specific RAG metrics; conversational grounding in dialogue; visual grounding; symbol grounding.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Linking generated or predicted content to source evidence at an appropriate granularity, such as passage, sentence, span, cell, region or document.
seed_audit.main_risk: Grounding location can be correct while the evidence is semantically insufficient, stale or incomplete.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Visual grounding without generated factual claims; entity grounding; knowledge-base entity linking.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: In RAG evaluation, commonly whether an answer's claims are supported by the retrieved context.
seed_audit.main_risk: The term is strongly tied to particular RAG metric frameworks and generally tests support, not retrieval completeness or temporal correctness.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Prompt-context adherence; dialogue-context consistency; framework-specific metric documentation without independent validation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Evaluation of whether all required, salient or reference-defined information is represented in an output.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase is extremely broad and its denominator is often undefined.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Database completeness, ontology completeness, software requirements completeness, dataset completeness, knowledge-graph completeness.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Measurement of how much relevant or required information, content units, evidence or instances are represented or answered.
seed_audit.main_risk: Coverage has incompatible meanings across summarization, retrieval, testing, selective prediction and networking.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Code coverage, wireless coverage, retrieval corpus coverage, test coverage, geographic coverage, generic dataset coverage.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Detection or measurement of relevant information that should have appeared in an output but is absent.
seed_audit.main_risk: Omission requires a defensible denominator of required information; many studies instead detect linguistic deletion or compare against a single reference.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Grammatical omission, word deletion detection, speech recognition deletion errors, translation omission without decision-relevance semantics.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Fine-grained semantic units used to represent summary content and evaluate salience or coverage at a more interpretable level than whole-summary overlap.
seed_audit.main_risk: ACUs concern content representation and salience; they do not by themselves establish source support, version validity or abstention.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Unrelated uses of ACU abbreviations; content-unit schemes that lack source-grounded factual assessment.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Evaluation in which individual propositions or semantic units, rather than whole documents or sentences, form the scoring units.
seed_audit.main_risk: A proposition may still be compound, context-dependent or temporally scoped, so proposition-level scoring does not automatically solve evidence completeness.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Logic proposition classification; proposition extraction for argument mining; semantic parsing without generation evaluation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Prediction with an explicit option to abstain, trading prediction coverage against error or risk.
seed_audit.main_risk: Most formal work assumes classification or structured prediction with readily defined correctness, unlike multi-dimensional free-form generation.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Image classification selective prediction with no transferable calibration analysis; active learning selection; selective sampling.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Classification with a reject or abstain mechanism, typically evaluated through coverage and conditional error or selective risk.
seed_audit.main_risk: It supplies foundational machinery but does not directly solve selective prediction for multi-claim generated text.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Vision-only classifiers; novelty rejection; outlier rejection without calibrated risk or downstream generation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Decision-theoretic option to withhold a prediction when expected error or cost is too high, historically studied through error-reject trade-offs.
seed_audit.main_risk: Foundational literature is mostly classification and pattern recognition, not language generation.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Engineering rejection mechanisms unrelated to statistical prediction; anomaly rejection with no coverage-risk formulation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Alignment between stated predictive probabilities or confidence and empirical frequencies of correctness.
seed_audit.main_risk: Free-form reports have multiple correctness dimensions, so a single confidence target can be ill-defined and hide denominator-specific failures.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Uncertainty estimation without calibration measurement; token entropy studies; model self-confidence studies without empirical correctness calibration.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A binned summary statistic comparing predicted confidence with empirical accuracy.
seed_audit.main_risk: ECE is estimator- and binning-dependent, can hide subgroup or local miscalibration and does not measure selective utility.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Papers reporting ECE for static image classification with no abstention, shift or language-generation connection.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A proper squared-error scoring rule for probabilistic predictions against observed outcomes.
seed_audit.main_risk: It requires a clearly defined probabilistic event; applying one Brier score to a report with several distinct error types would collapse required denominators.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Weather forecasting or binary classification applications with no methodological transfer beyond the scoring rule.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Curve showing conditional prediction risk as progressively fewer examples are answered under an abstention or selection rule.
seed_audit.main_risk: The risk function must be defined correctly; one aggregate report-level risk can conceal unsupported claims or omission failures.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Coverage curves unrelated to abstention; coverage probability plots; recall-coverage visualizations.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Expected loss conditional on the system choosing to issue a prediction rather than abstaining.
seed_audit.main_risk: A scalar loss may hide asymmetric and dimension-specific errors unless selective risk is reported separately for each relevant outcome.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Portfolio risk selection; feature-selection risk; unrelated decision-risk literature.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Explicit refusal or deferral of a prediction when confidence, evidence or expected utility is inadequate.
seed_audit.main_risk: Natural-language refusal behavior is not automatically a calibrated abstention policy, and excessive abstention can achieve low error by destroying useful coverage.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Safety refusal taxonomies with no quantitative risk-coverage analysis; political abstention; voting abstention.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Framework for producing prediction sets or intervals with coverage guarantees under specified assumptions, with later variants adapting to online or distribution-shift settings.
seed_audit.main_risk: Standard guarantees generally assume exchangeability or structured outcomes; direct transfer to non-stationary free-form reports and multiple semantic failure dimensions is not automatic.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Static regression intervals; image classification prediction sets; exchangeable-data studies with no treatment of drift or generated text.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Measurement of consistency among human annotators applying an annotation or evaluation protocol.
seed_audit.main_risk: Agreement is not correctness, and a high agreement coefficient does not guarantee valid labels or adequate coverage of rare high-risk cases.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Generic annotation studies unrelated to generation reliability; studies reporting only kappa without adjudication or construct validation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Study of reproducibility, agreement, protocol quality, annotator variability and validity in human judgments of generated outputs.
seed_audit.main_risk: Generic preference evaluation may not support evidence-level correctness, omission or calibrated abstention labels.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Fluency/preference-only human evaluation; crowdsourcing studies with no factual or evidence-grounding task.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Evaluation of retrieval and generation components, commonly separating retrieval relevance/recall, answer correctness and faithfulness or grounding.
seed_audit.main_risk: Many RAG frameworks conflate retrieved-context quality with evidence sufficiency, use proprietary LLM judges, or do not evaluate omissions and temporal versions.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: RAG system accuracy studies reporting only answer score; retrieval-only benchmarks; framework marketing material without human validation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: A diffuse term covering evaluation or optimization according to downstream decision consequences, utility, task success or decision quality rather than generic predictive accuracy.
seed_audit.main_risk: The dominant phrase can refer to decision-focused learning or predict-then-optimize rather than evaluation of generated reports.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Operations-research decision-focused learning, differentiable optimization, policy learning and downstream optimization without evidence-grounded generation.

task_families.name: Claim-level factual consistency and faithfulness
task_families.description: Decompose or inspect generated text and determine whether each factual statement is supported by its source evidence.
task_families.why_it_matters: Provides the claim-correctness denominator needed by the integrated framework without confusing correctness with attribution or completeness.
seed_papers: Evaluating the Factual Consistency of Abstractive Text Summarization — Kryscinski et al. (2020)
Asking and Answering Questions to Evaluate the Factual Consistency of Summaries — Wang, Cho and Lewis (2020)
SummaC: Re-Visiting NLI-based Models for Inconsistency Detection in Summarization — Laban et al. (2022)
TRUE: Re-evaluating Factual Consistency Evaluation — Honovich et al. (2022)

task_families.name: Atomic claim and content-unit decomposition
task_families.description: Represent long-form output as atomic facts, propositions, semantic content units or other independently scorable units.
task_families.why_it_matters: Compound generated sentences must not receive one binary label when different subclaims have different evidence, temporal status or citations.
seed_papers: Evaluating Content Selection in Summarization: The Pyramid Method — Nenkova and Passonneau (2004)
Revisiting the Gold Standard: Grounding Summarization Evaluation with Robust Human Evaluation — Liu et al. (2023)
FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation — Min et al. (2023)
ACUEval: Fine-grained Hallucination Evaluation and Correction for Abstractive Summarization — Wan et al. (2024)

task_families.name: Attribution and citation correctness
task_families.description: Determine whether each cited or identified source genuinely supports the generated claim to which it is attached.
task_families.why_it_matters: msgloom requires claim correctness and source-attribution correctness to remain separate outcomes.
seed_papers: Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models — Rashkin et al. (2023)
Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations — Gao et al. (2023)

task_families.name: Evidence completeness, citation recall and multi-source sufficiency
task_families.description: Measure whether every evidence-requiring claim has all evidence needed for its full semantics, including compound claims, partial support and complementary sources.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the main search family for gap-4. It must distinguish a correct citation from complete evidentiary support and seek methods handling multiple evidence pieces.
seed_papers: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations — Gao et al. (2023)

task_families.name: Content coverage, salience and omission evaluation
task_families.description: Define required information units and measure whether generated summaries or reports omit important source content.
task_families.why_it_matters: This supplies the denominator for report-level omission and complements factual precision, which does not penalize a system for saying too little.
seed_papers: Evaluating Content Selection in Summarization: The Pyramid Method — Nenkova and Passonneau (2004)
Revisiting the Gold Standard: Grounding Summarization Evaluation with Robust Human Evaluation — Liu et al. (2023)

task_families.name: Update, temporal and longitudinal summarization evaluation
task_families.description: Evaluate summaries of information streams that evolve through successive batches, with emphasis on novelty, content coverage, chronology and what the reader already knows.
task_families.why_it_matters: It is the closest established task family for gap-5's repeated-cycle briefing problem and can expose terminology for new, changed, stale or omitted information, although workplace work-item semantics remain project-specific.
seed_papers: TAC 2008 Update Summarization Task and its overview literature

task_families.name: Integrated multidimensional evaluation and meta-evaluation
task_families.description: Frameworks or benchmarks that deliberately keep factual correctness, attribution, completeness, temporal validity, uncertainty and abstention as distinguishable evaluation dimensions.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the main family for gap-1. Discovery should look for combined frameworks but reject papers that collapse the dimensions into one score.
seed_papers: TRUE: Re-evaluating Factual Consistency Evaluation — Honovich et al. (2022)
Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models — Rashkin et al. (2023)
Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations — Gao et al. (2023)

task_families.name: Selective prediction and abstention in NLP
task_families.description: Allow an NLP system to withhold low-confidence predictions and evaluate conditional error against retained coverage.
task_families.why_it_matters: The risk-coverage formalism is highly relevant, but most validated tasks are classification or structured NLP rather than multi-dimensional free-form reports.
seed_papers: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks — Geifman and El-Yaniv (2017)
The Art of Abstention: Selective Prediction and Error Regularization for Natural Language Processing — Xin et al. (2021)

task_families.name: Probability calibration and proper scoring
task_families.description: Assess whether confidence values correspond to empirical correctness probabilities using reliability analysis and proper scoring rules.
task_families.why_it_matters: Provides calibration machinery, but msgloom must define separate probabilistic targets for different semantic error dimensions instead of assigning one confidence to an entire report.
seed_papers: Verification of Forecasts Expressed in Terms of Probability — Brier (1950)
On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks — Guo et al. (2017)

task_families.name: Reject-option decision theory and risk-coverage analysis
task_families.description: Study optimal or empirical trade-offs between making predictions and rejecting or deferring them.
task_families.why_it_matters: Supplies the conceptual foundation for abstention costs, useful coverage and selective risk.
seed_papers: On Optimum Recognition Error and Reject Tradeoff — Chow (1970)
Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks — Geifman and El-Yaniv (2017)

task_families.name: Online calibration and conformal prediction under distribution shift
task_families.description: Maintain calibration or coverage when the generating distribution evolves over time, including adaptive and online conformal methods.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the principal methodological search family for gap-8. The key question is whether any method extends from structured outcomes to free-form communication reliability without invalidating its assumptions.
seed_papers: Algorithmic Learning in a Random World — Vovk, Gammerman and Shafer (2005)
A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction — Shafer and Vovk (2008)
Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift — Gibbs and Candes (2021)
Conformal Inference for Online Prediction with Arbitrary Distribution Shifts — Gibbs and Candes (2024)

task_families.name: Human evaluation reliability and evaluator meta-evaluation
task_families.description: Validate annotation protocols, human agreement, adjudication and automatic or LLM evaluators against independent human judgments.
task_families.why_it_matters: Supports methodology around gap-6 and gap-7 while leaving sample size, risk stratification, acceptance policy and evaluator separation as engineering decisions.
seed_papers: Revisiting the Gold Standard: Grounding Summarization Evaluation with Robust Human Evaluation — Liu et al. (2023)

task_families.name: Longitudinal workplace communication and briefing benchmarks
task_families.description: Direct evaluation on email, enterprise messaging or comparable communication where facts and work items change across threads, revisions and observation cutoffs.
task_families.why_it_matters: A bounded search may find a previously missed direct benchmark for gap-2 or gap-5. Ordinary email summarization is insufficient unless it includes the required longitudinal, revision and omission semantics.

task_families.name: Decision-focused and utility-sensitive evaluation
task_families.description: Evaluate errors according to downstream decision consequences, asymmetric loss or task utility rather than treating every error as equally costly.
task_families.why_it_matters: Useful for prioritizing missed due work, false completion, unsupported action claims and abstention, but generic decision-focused learning must not be mistaken for a report-evaluation framework.

queries: "factual consistency" evaluation summarization generated claims source evidence
"faithfulness evaluation" summarization source grounded factual consistency
"factual consistency metric" grounded generation human evaluation
"citation completeness" multiple evidence passages long-form generation
"evaluation framework" factuality attribution "evidence completeness" temporal correctness omission uncertainty abstention "free-form generation"
"multi-dimensional evaluation" grounded generation factuality attribution completeness uncertainty
"evaluation framework" "citation completeness" factuality abstention calibration generation
"benchmark" factuality attribution citation recall abstention calibration "long-form generation"
"generation evaluation" factuality attribution completeness omission calibration
"reliability evaluation" free-form generation attribution completeness abstention
"selective prediction" non-stationary stream distribution shift calibration abstention
"LLM judge" factuality evaluation human agreement bias
"automatic evaluator" bias generation evaluation human validation
"email" summarization revisions quoted history conflicting information

demoted_terms: hallucination evaluation when used without a precise error taxonomy
groundedness as a single aggregate score
coverage evaluation without a named denominator
completeness evaluation without a named information unit
context faithfulness as a substitute for evidence completeness
expected calibration error as a complete calibration assessment
model confidence as a substitute for calibrated probability
conformal prediction as if its guarantees automatically transfer to free-form generation
decision-focused evaluation without utility or loss semantics
citation presence as a substitute for citation correctness
generic RAG evaluation as a substitute for decomposed reliability evaluation
downgrade_rules: Downgrade any paper that reports only one aggregate factuality, faithfulness, hallucination or groundedness score when it does not preserve separate denominators for factual correctness, attribution and completeness.
Downgrade citation work that checks whether a citation exists but does not test whether it supports the associated claim.
Downgrade citation-correctness work as insufficient for gap-4 when it does not also evaluate missing citations or missing complementary evidence.
Downgrade evidence-completeness claims when a compound claim is treated as fully supported by one source that supports only part of the proposition.
Downgrade multi-source retrieval recall when it measures whether relevant passages were retrieved but never tests whether the generated claim used all necessary evidence.
Downgrade fact-verification studies with static claims and static evidence to TRANSFER unless their evaluation machinery explicitly addresses generated claims, attribution or evidence sufficiency.
Downgrade ordinary static summarization studies for gap-5 unless they evaluate changing information, prior-reader state, updates, chronology or longitudinal content.
Downgrade update or temporal summarization work as insufficient for gap-5 when it measures only novelty or redundancy and never measures omission of important evolving state.
Downgrade timeline summarization based only on event ordering when it does not evaluate missing decision-relevant information or superseded facts.

Downgrade workplace or email summarization benchmarks for gap-2 unless they contain realistic longitudinal revisions, quoted or forwarded history, conflicting updates, out-of-order arrival or comparable evidence-version semantics.
Do not treat synthetic, public-news or QA results as evidence of production workplace accuracy; they may validate transfer methodology only.

Downgrade calibration studies that equate raw model probability, token probability, entropy or verbal self-confidence with calibrated probability without empirical calibration against the relevant outcome.
Downgrade papers reporting only ECE when they do not inspect reliability across useful operating ranges, subgroups or selective coverage where those are material.
Downgrade low-error abstention systems that achieve reliability mainly by abstaining on almost everything; useful coverage and risk must be reported together.
Downgrade selective-classification results to TRANSFER when the output is a single class and there is no evidence that the selection mechanism remains valid for free-form multi-claim outputs.
Downgrade standard conformal prediction to TRANSFER when its guarantee assumes exchangeability or a static distribution that is violated by the target non-stationary stream.
Do not treat conformal coverage of a classification label or numeric interval as direct evidence of calibrated semantic correctness, evidence completeness or report omission.
Downgrade distribution-shift papers that evaluate one fixed shift or domain transfer but not continuing online or temporal change for gap-8.
Downgrade human-evaluation papers that report inter-annotator agreement alone; agreement is not evidence of label validity, representative sampling or adequate rare-risk coverage.
Downgrade LLM-as-judge papers that do not validate the judge against independent human or ground-truth judgments on the dimensions being scored.
Downgrade evaluator-bias findings as insufficient for gap-7 when they do not inform independent test separation, holdout evaluation or regression procedures; those remain engineering controls.

Reject authorship attribution, plagiarism attribution and news-source classification returned by the phrase source attribution unless the paper also evaluates generated statements against supporting evidence.
Reject code coverage, wireless coverage, geographic coverage and test-coverage literature returned by coverage evaluation.
Reject grammatical omission, translation deletion or speech-recognition deletion work for gap-5 unless its method explicitly transfers to semantic information omission.
Reject decision-focused learning or predict-then-optimize papers returned by decision-focused evaluation unless they contribute an evaluation or asymmetric-risk method relevant to generated outputs.
Do not count multiple records of the same underlying study as independent corroborating papers.

date_policy.rationale: Discovery must not impose a modern-LLM-only window. The calibration branch includes Glenn W. Brier's 1950 probability-forecast verification work underlying the Brier score; reject-option theory has foundational work by Chow in the 1950s and 1970; content-unit summarization evaluation includes the Pyramid Method from 2004; conformal prediction developed before the current LLM era; and modern factuality, attribution and citation evaluation accelerated mainly after 2020. Use 1950 as the hard earliest year, while ranking recent direct generation literature higher. Queries should remain task-qualified so the older window does not turn discovery into a generic statistics survey.
